32.0.0.en: The time of the prophecy is given as the tenth year of King Zedekiah of Judah, which corresponds to the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, that is, the year 588 BC.

32.1.0.en: At the time of this prophecy, which God sent to Jeremiah, Jerusalem was besieged by the armies of Babylon. They then withdrew for a short time as the armies of Egypt advanced toward Jerusalem, after which Babylon returned and besieged Jerusalem with the final siege, then destroyed it and completed the last captivity of the Jews.

32.1.1.en: At this time Jeremiah was imprisoned in a special prison belonging to the palace of the king of Judah, and he had some freedom of movement, as is shown by his weighing out the silver and buying the land in his town of Anathoth. Although this prison was hard for Jeremiah as an affliction, it was an opportunity to keep Jeremiah safe from the abuse of his enemies and a protection for him.

32.2.0.en: The reason for Jeremiah's imprisonment was the anger of Zedekiah king of Judah against him, because he had prophesied several things. The first was that the king of Babylon would take Jerusalem.

32.3.0.en: Jeremiah continues his prophecy and announces a second matter, that the king of Babylon would seize Zedekiah king of Judah.

32.3.1.en: And a third prophecy, that Zedekiah would meet the king of Babylon.

32.4.0.en: Jeremiah adds to his prophecy a fourth matter, that the Chaldeans, that is, the Babylonians, would carry King Zedekiah away to Babylon. He says “carry” because they would put out his eyes and lead him to Babylon, which he would not see, as the prophet Ezekiel said (Ezek 12:13), but he would remain there for the rest of his life.

32.4.1.en: And he prophesies a fifth matter, that Zedekiah would remain in Babylon until the end of his life, where God would visit him, that is, he would die and be removed from our land.

32.4.2.en: A sixth and last prophecy that Jeremiah spoke is that Judah's attempt to resist Babylon would fail, and Babylon would kill many of the Jews, take captive those it chose, and leave the weak in the land.

32.4.3.en: In the afflictions that God allows for you, His love and care for you are hidden. Just as Jeremiah was imprisoned in the palace of the king of Judah to protect him from his enemies, so God also protects you from many troubles by means of the afflictions that you pass through. So thank God for everything, even afflictions.

32.5.0.en: God commanded Jeremiah to buy a field in his town of Anathoth, where he and his family were born and lived, a town of the priests near Jerusalem. It appears that Jeremiah's cousin, who owned this field, had fallen into financial difficulty and so had mortgaged it. To preserve the inheritance of the land, one of his relatives could buy the field so that it would remain the property of the family, as the Law stipulated in (Lev 25:25), because the Promised Land was a type of the heavenly Jerusalem, which is the eternal inheritance, and so it must be preserved.

32.5.1.en: It appears that Jeremiah's cousin did not find anyone to buy this field from the person with whom it had been mortgaged and to pay the price of redeeming it and returning it to the family. Perhaps this was because of the captivity that was coming upon them, and therefore there was no benefit in such a purchase, since Babylon would take possession of all the lands. So he came to Jeremiah in the prison and offered him the field to buy, in order to restore the inheritance to the family.

32.5.2.en: Shallum was Jeremiah's uncle and Hanamel was his cousin.

32.5.3.en: God had informed Jeremiah of Hanamel's coming to him before he arrived, and commanded him to buy the land.

32.5.4.en: Here God uses a visual aid to declare before the Jews that the captivity would come but that they would return from it. So He had His prophet Jeremiah buy the field as a confirmation that their return from the captivity was certain. It is a clear hope and a consolation that God offers to His children.

32.5.5.en: If God allows afflictions for you, He shows you at the same time His power and His care for you. So do not be grieved because of the affliction, but seek God, and He will show you His presence with you, and your heart will be comforted.

32.6.0.en: God's word was fulfilled when Hanamel, Jeremiah's cousin, arrived at the prison where Jeremiah was held, and offered him to redeem his mortgaged field and to buy it for himself so that it would return to the ownership of the family. So Jeremiah was assured of what God had told him beforehand.

32.6.1.en: For God prepares and guides His children who cling to Him, so that they are not troubled by the events coming upon them, and when they are reassured they become an example to those around them.

32.6.2.en: From another side, God guides His children in the details of their lives as long as they hold fast to Him.

32.7.0.en: A shekel of silver: equal to about fifteen grams.

32.7.1.en: Jeremiah obeyed God's word and bought his cousin's field, and paid him its price, which was seventeen shekels of silver.

32.8.0.en: Jeremiah wrote a deed for the purchase of the field in order to establish his ownership of it, and this was done before witnesses, both from the relatives who came with Hanamel and from those imprisoned with him.

32.8.1.en: He sealed this deed, that is, the contract, and weighed the silver before the witnesses as proof of his ownership.

32.9.0.en: The custom in buying in ancient times was to write two copies of the contract, either both exactly identical or one a summary of the other. One was closed and sealed, while the other remained open, to confirm ownership.

32.10.0.en: After the witnesses had signed the deed of purchase and Hanamel had received the price, Jeremiah gave the deed to his disciple “Baruch,” who was the scribe of his prophecies and helped him in writing any matters that concerned him. All this was as proof before many witnesses, and a declaration to the people that Jeremiah had bought a field even though Babylon was besieging Jerusalem and the captivity was drawing near them, in order to declare, as we mentioned, that they would return from the captivity and enjoy their lands.

32.11.0.en: Baruch, the disciple of Jeremiah, was also a prophet, and he has a prophecy in his name among the canonical books, which the Protestants removed.

32.11.1.en: Jeremiah commanded him to put the two copies of the deed in an earthen vessel. This was the custom for preserving important documents: they were placed in an earthen vessel, which was closed over them and the seal was fixed with pitch. This was a declaration from Jeremiah that the captivity would last for many years, but that after it the Jews would return from the captivity.

32.12.0.en: God confirms the return from the captivity and the Jews' buying of houses and fields.

32.12.1.en: All this is a type of Christ, who bought us with His blood and wrote the deed on the Cross. The accomplishment of complete salvation will come after the years of our earthly life, when we are lifted up to the heavenly Jerusalem and reign with Him forever. The two copies of the contract of purchase signify, the open one, the blessings that we receive now on earth, and the sealed one, the blessings that we shall receive in heaven, which cannot be expressed. Christ took our nature by His Incarnation to be near to us and to complete our redemption, so that He frees us from the hand of Satan, to whom we sold ourselves because of our spiritual poverty. The price of redemption was paid openly before many witnesses, namely all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, outside which Christ was crucified.

32.12.3.en: 16- Now when I had delivered the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch the son of Neriah, I prayed unto the LORD, saying, 17- Ah Lord GOD! behold, thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee: 18- Thou shewest lovingkindness unto thousands, and recompensest the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them: the Great, the Mighty God, the LORD of hosts, is his name, 19- Great in counsel, and mighty in work: for thine eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of men: to give every one according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings: 20- Which hast set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, even unto this day, and in Israel, and among other men; and hast made thee a name, as at this day;

32.12.4.en: 21- And hast brought forth thy people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs, and with wonders, and with a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with great terror; 22- And hast given them this land, which thou didst swear to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey;

32.12.5.en: 23- And they came in, and possessed it; but they obeyed not thy voice, neither walked in thy law; they have done nothing of all that thou commandedst them to do: therefore thou hast caused all this evil to come upon them: 24- Behold the mounts, they are come unto the city to take it; and the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans, that fight against it, because of the sword, and of the famine, and of the pestilence: and what thou hast spoken is come to pass; and, behold, thou seest it. 25- And thou hast said unto me, O Lord GOD, Buy thee the field for money, and take witnesses; for the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.

32.13.0.en: After the procedures for buying the field were finished, Jeremiah stood to pray. This was his first concern; indeed, the goal of all the matters of his life was his attachment to God. In his prayer he reviews God's kindnesses and His provisions for His people and His care for them even in afflictions.

32.13.1.en: At the beginning of his prayer he glorifies God, the Creator of all things, and also describes Him as the One who is able to do all things.

32.14.0.en: He describes God by the love that appears in His gifts to His people, who number in the thousands, for He cares for all His children. Then he presents a fourth attribute of God, which is His justice, which appears in His recompense, not only to the wicked fathers but also to their children if they walk in the sins of their fathers.

32.14.1.en: He describes a fifth attribute of God, that He is strong and mighty, and calls Him “the LORD of hosts” to show His power. Let us notice that Jeremiah's prayer is praise of God and a review of His many attributes, for praise is love of God and attachment to Him.

32.15.0.en: He continues his praise of God and describes Him with a sixth attribute, His greatness in guiding His children. His counsel is the true counsel, because He knows everything and loves His children.

32.15.1.en: Then he describes Him with a seventh attribute, His knowledge of everything, which he expresses by saying that His eyes are open upon all that happens on the earth. This reassures His children and those who fear Him, since He protects them and blesses them, and at the same time it troubles the wicked, because He will punish them for their sins.

32.16.0.en: He reminds God of His power by which He saved His people when they were enslaved in Egypt, when He struck the Egyptians with the ten plagues, brought them through the Red Sea, and destroyed the army of the Egyptians. So he praises His divine power and His care for His people, of which the whole world has spoken to this day, because what happened will never be erased from the minds of men because of its greatness.

32.17.0.en: He thanks God, who fulfilled His promises to Abraham and the fathers. This is an eighth attribute of God, the truthfulness of His promises, since He gave His people to possess the land of Canaan, which was full of good things.

32.18.0.en: Jeremiah makes a confession before God, on behalf of his people, that after they possessed the land of Canaan they left God's commandments and walked in their evil lusts, so they deserved that God should punish them with the captivity, that is, with this evil.

32.19.0.en: The mounts: the soldiers who build the siege mounds. The word is the plural of a mound, which is a wall of brick or stones, or any obstacles that the enemies build around besieged cities to hinder the fighting of the besieged if they try to escape.

32.19.3.en: After that he declares the truthfulness of God in His word that He sent to Jeremiah to proclaim as prophecies before the people. For God had said that Jerusalem would be besieged by the Babylonians and would fall into their hands, not only because of the Babylonians' cruelty in killing the Jews, but also because of the Jews' weakness, as diseases attacked them and they found no food to eat during the siege. All this was a discipline from God for His people who had rebelled against Him.

32.19.4.en: Thus a ninth attribute of God appears, which Jeremiah praises, namely the truthfulness of His word and His prophecies.

32.20.0.en: He praises God, who comforts His people, which is a tenth attribute in God, for He gave them hope of returning from the captivity and presented to them a real story, namely Jeremiah's buying of a field even though Babylon would shortly take possession of the whole kingdom of Judah, yet they would return and enjoy their lands. Jeremiah did not benefit from this land because he died before the return from the captivity, but he obeyed so as to declare by this act the love of God, who would bring His people back from the captivity.

32.20.1.en: How beautiful it is for you to contemplate the attributes of God, and to praise Him and thank Him for His gifts and care. May you learn even a small part of the Church's Midnight Praise (Tasbeha), or listen to it on recordings, to take part in praising His holy name, and your heart will be filled with joy.

32.20.3.en: 26- Then came the word of the LORD unto Jeremiah, saying, 27- Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me? 28- Therefore thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he shall take it: 29- And the Chaldeans, that fight against this city, shall come and set fire on this city, and burn it with the houses, upon whose roofs they have offered incense unto Baal, and poured out drink offerings unto other gods, to provoke me to anger. 30- For the children of Israel and the children of Judah have only done evil before me from their youth: for the children of Israel have only provoked me to anger with the work of their hands, saith the LORD. 31- For this city hath been to me as a provocation of mine anger and of my fury from the day that they built it even unto this day; that I should remove it from before my face, 32- Because of all the evil of the children of Israel and of the children of Judah, which they have done to provoke me to anger, they, their kings, their princes, their priests, and their prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

32.20.4.en: 33- And they have turned unto me the back, and not the face: though I taught them, rising up early and teaching them, yet they have not hearkened to receive instruction.

32.20.5.en: 34- But they set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name, to defile it. 35- And they built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my mind, that they should do this abomination, to cause Judah to sin.

32.21.0.en: After God listened to Jeremiah's prayer, He declared to him that He is the Creator of all creatures and able to do all things, and that He disciplines His people so that they repent, then brings them back from the captivity and comforts their hearts.

32.22.0.en: God carries out His discipline by allowing Babylon to take Jerusalem.

32.23.0.en: God continues His words by saying that Babylon would burn Jerusalem and its houses, on whose roofs the Jews had worshiped idols.

32.23.1.en: Here He begins to show the reasons for His discipline of His people. The first is their worship of idols on the roofs of their houses, that is, their worship of the heavenly bodies.

32.24.0.en: The second reason for God's discipline of His people is their continuing in evil for a long time. They began it from their youth and not only now, for they worshiped idols from the time they were in Egypt, even before they entered Egypt, and God bore with them throughout this long period so that they would repent.

32.25.0.en: He adds a third reason for the discipline of Jerusalem, that it worshiped idols and walked in evil from the time when the Jebusites, the original pagan inhabitants of the land, lived in it. Then after the Jews possessed it, they completed the evil in it, so Jerusalem deserved to be destroyed at the hand of Babylon.

32.26.0.en: A fourth reason for the discipline of God's people is that everyone shared in the evil, the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Israel, the leaders such as the kings and the ordinary people. This evil is directed against God, a provocation to Him, and disobedience and defiance.

32.27.0.en: The fifth reason for the discipline is the insistence on not obeying God and hearkening to His commandments, and even treating Him with neglect and coldness, which is expressed by giving God the back and not the face.

32.27.1.en: Take care lest you fall into neglect of God and give Him the back and not the face, when you neglect your prayer, or your reading of the Holy Bible, or coming to the house of God.

32.28.0.en: The sixth reason for the discipline is the audacity of placing idol images inside God's temple in Jerusalem, for this is the utmost defiance of God.

32.29.0.en: The seventh reason for the discipline is their loss of natural human affection, for in their immersion in the worship of the pagan gods they offered their sons to them as burnt offerings, like the god Molech, and sacrificed their children out of love for idol worship, in addition to building temples for the worship of the god Molech on the hills and high places.

32.29.2.en: 36- And now therefore thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning this city, whereof ye say, It shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence; 37- Behold, I will gather them out of all countries, whither I have driven them in mine anger, and in my fury, and in great wrath; and I will bring them again unto this place, and I will cause them to dwell safely: 38- And they shall be my people, and I will be their God: 39- And I will give them one heart, and one way, that they may fear me for ever, for the good of them, and of their children after them: 40- And I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from them, to do them good; but I will put my fear in their hearts, that they shall not depart from me. 41- Yea, I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land assuredly with my whole heart and with my whole soul. 42- For thus saith the LORD; Like as I have brought all this great evil upon this people, so will I bring upon them all the good that I have promised them. 43- And fields shall be bought in this land, whereof ye say, It is desolate without man or beast; it is given into the hand of the Chaldeans. 44- Men shall buy fields for money, and subscribe evidences, and seal them, and take witnesses in the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, and in the cities of the mountains, and in the cities of the valley, and in the cities of the south: for I will cause their captivity to return, saith the LORD.

32.30.1.en: Although God allows His people to be disciplined by the captivity, with all the killing, hunger and disease that it brings, when He finds His people accepting the discipline He returns and has mercy on them and brings them back from the captivity. For God is not cruel but a tender Father who disciplines His children so that they repent and return to His embrace.

32.31.0.en: God promises to gather His people who were scattered in the captivity, and then to bring them back to their land, and more than that, that they will live in security in their land, because when they repent they obtain all mercies.

32.31.1.en: God's mercies are waiting for you to repent of your sins, and they will pour out upon you countless blessings. So do not delay repentance, and do not despair because of the multitude of your sins, and do not be led away after passing pleasures.

32.32.0.en: God makes a fourth promise, that He will give His people the enjoyment of special care because they believe in Him, and He will reign over their hearts.

32.33.0.en: The fifth promise is the unity that He gives to His people, so that the division of the two kingdoms, Israel and Judah, ends. This is a type of unity in Christ, where the believers in the whole world are united in Christ. The sixth promise is that God gives them His fear in their hearts, so that they reject sin and enjoy His abundant goodness.

32.34.0.en: The seventh promise is God's care for His children forever, so that He establishes His fear in their hearts, and good things continue for them as long as they believe in Him and hold fast to His commandments. This is fulfilled in Christ, who gives us the eternal Kingdom.

32.35.0.en: The eighth promise that God gives His people after their return from the captivity is that He will establish them in faithfulness and upright conduct toward Him and toward one another, and God will work in them with all power and rejoice in their response to Him. This is the true divine kindness, not only material good things but faithfulness in carrying out His commandments.

32.36.0.en: Thus, in proportion to the discipline and afflictions they endured in the captivity, God compensates them after the return from the captivity with many good things.

32.37.0.en: The ninth promise is the fertility of the land that had been desolate, so that the Jews eagerly buy it to enjoy its good things.

32.38.0.en: He confirms their concern for the process of buying fields with all its procedures, including writing documents for this purchase and sealing them with seals. That is, the land is of great value, so they make sure of their ownership of it after paying high prices for it in silver and gold. This would be not only in Jerusalem but in all the regions around it in the tribes of Judah and Benjamin. This signifies the enlightenment of the believers in the New Testament and their concern to buy the new land, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven, and to exert every effort to acquire it through their worship in the Church and their spiritual striving.

32.38.1.en: God's blessings for those who obey Him
